headline: We've crossed out of the rap albums into the electronic Singles crate — house tempos and major keys are climbing on cue — and the analysis surfaced one real data-quality issue with vocal detection.
insights: Into the Singles crate. ~103 electronic tracks analyzed and the shift is visible: the 120–129 BPM house band now holds 180 tracks, up from essentially zero at cycle 1. Prodigy, Moodymann, DJ Koze, Soft Cell are all in the DB.
Keys are opening up. Major-key (Camelot B) share has climbed to 34% (285 of 827) from the near-total minor of the opening trap block — dance material brings brighter keys, exactly as predicted.

⚠ The vocal flag is unreliable. It reads 92% of the electronic Singles as "vocal", including clear instrumentals (Moodymann – People, Prodigy – Out of Space). The harmonic/percussive heuristic conflates any tonal content with vocals. Impact is contained: the "don't stack two vocals" guard becomes inert, so I'll de-weight it in the final sequencing — BPM, key and energy ordering are unaffected.
Throughput steady at 23.8 tracks/min. 25% done, ETA ~1h40m, tracking to finish around 00:40. Just 1 decode failure so far (Huncho Jack – "Eye 2 Eye", a FLAC) out of 828 = 0.1%.

Singles energy (0.53) sits just under the album block (0.56) — the crate-dig material so far is groove-driven, not peak-time. Expect energy and the major-key share to keep rising as the run reaches the tech-house, UKG and baile-edit material deeper in the 923-track Singles folder.
roadblocks_note: Vocal heuristic over-fires (~92–98% everywhere) → flagged for de-weighting in final sequencing; not blocking. 1 decode failure (Huncho Jack 'Eye 2 Eye'). Benign librosa PySoundFile→audioread fallback for m4a/mp3 continues. Device steady, 0 pull failures, 9 workers live.
next: Going deeper into Singles: watch the 120–128 house spike and the 130–150 UKG/baile bands swell, and energy + major-key share keep climbing.
